title: PMT vs IPMT vs PPMT
description: Understand the difference between total payment, interest portion, and principal portion of a loan.
intro: PMT calculates the total periodic payment on a loan. IPMT and PPMT split that payment into the interest and principal portions for a specific period.

comparisonTable.functionB: Interest portion of a specific payment
comparisonTable.functionC: Principal portion of a specific payment

whenToUseA: Use PMT when you need to know the total periodic payment amount for budgeting or loan qualification.
whenToUseB: Use IPMT when building an amortization schedule or analyzing interest expense in a specific period.
whenToUseC: Use PPMT when tracking principal repayment or calculating remaining loan balance.
verdict: These functions work together: PMT gives the total payment, while IPMT and PPMT split it into interest and principal.

faq.question: Why are IPMT and PPMT negative?
faq.answer: They represent cash outflows. Multiply by -1 or use ABS for positive values.

faq.question: Does PMT equal IPMT plus PPMT?
faq.answer: Yes, for a fixed-rate loan, PMT = IPMT + PPMT for the same period.
